dedupe_keys.name: texas winter deep freeze of february 2021 and refining and petrochemical supply chains dallas fed

description: This case study, an article in the Dallas Fed's Southwest Economy by Jesse Thompson, analyses how the record Arctic cold of mid-February 2021 hit the Texas refining and petrochemical industry as hard as a hurricane. Power producers that had not winterised their plants failed, the Electric Reliability Council of Texas ordered rolling blackouts, and the combined loss of electricity, raw materials and the cold itself forced rapid shutdowns of refineries and chemical plants that took weeks to unwind, with operations not fully back until early April. It was produced by the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas. Coverage is Texas and the Gulf Coast, drawing on Energy Information Administration refinery data, chemical railcar loadings, which fell 28% in one week, and prices, with ethylene up 78% from December 2020 to March 2021 and high-density polyethylene up 61%. The article is available free online with downloadable charts; no licence is stated. Caveats: it is a short economic analysis written in 2021, so recovery estimates were projections, and it gives no plant-level detail. For simulation it documents a cascade from power outages to industrial shutdowns, product shortages and price spikes, useful for calibrating interdependency and supply chain models of energy and chemical infrastructure under extreme cold. It is related to the Texas February 2021 winter storm blackout case study in this catalogue.
